office_does: The Superior Court clerk keeps the county court's records and filings, runs jury administration, and collects court fines, fees and restitution.
race_blurb: Incumbent Jenn Biggar, appointed in 2021 and elected unopposed in 2022, faces court facilitator and former deputy clerk Andrea Jester. Biggar runs on modernizing the office; Jester on customer service and staff retention, with the endorsement of the union representing the office's staff. Biggar led the primary 5,285 to 3,812.

candidates.summary: Douglas County Clerk since her 2021 appointment, elected unopposed in 2022, and incoming president of the Washington State Association of County Clerks.
highlights: Says she recovered about $90,000 from the state while refunding legal financial obligations after State v. Blake [S3]
Implemented the TrueFile electronic filing system in 2023 and put court calendars and Zoom links online [S3]
Plans a new jury system with electronic responses and text reminders [S3]
Endorsed by retired Judge John Hotchkiss, retired Clerk Tristen Worthen and county clerks statewide [S4]

experience.basis: Five-year incumbent, appointed in 2021 and elected in 2022, running on her record in office.

candidates.summary: Douglas County court facilitator and former deputy clerk and jury administrator, also administrative director and EMT with Waterville EMS.
highlights: Would focus on customer service, staff training and retention, and consistent procedures [S1][S2]
Says 'high turnover creates inconsistency and frustration for both staff and the public' [S2]
Endorsed by AFSCME Council 2 Local 846-DC, which represents the Clerk's Office staff [S1][S3]
Has worked in the court as deputy clerk, jury program administrator and financial collections officer [S2]

experience.basis: Challenger seeking change in how the office is run, though her experience comes from inside the same court system.
